description: A Radar or Web Chart is a graphical method of displaying multivariate data simultaneously. In competitive exams, it is primarily used to compare the performance of two or more entities across various parameters.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: Understanding the main components of a radar chart, which is essential for accurately reading the data.

key_concepts.explanation: This is the origin point from where all axes begin. Its baseline value is typically zero.
Lines radiating outwards from the center point, each representing a different category or parameter.
Polygons or circles formed around the center that represent the measurement scale or specific data increments.

sections.title: Common Calculation Formulas
sections.description: Fundamental mathematical formulas frequently required to solve Data Interpretation questions based on these charts.

equations: What percent of B is A = (A / B) * 100
Ratio of A to B = A / B
Average = (Sum of all observations) / (Total number of observations)

sections.title: Steps to Extract Data
sections.description: A systematic approach to accurately interpreting and extracting numerical values from a Radar Chart.

steps.title: Understand the Scale
steps.detail: Determine the value gap between consecutive concentric grid lines. For instance, each grid interval might represent 5, 10, or 20 units.

steps.title: Identify the Parameter
steps.detail: Locate the specific axis or radius corresponding to the entity or category mentioned in the question.

steps.title: Locate the Data Point
steps.detail: Find where the data plot intersects the identified axis and use the grid lines to calculate its exact numerical value.

sections.title: Common Scenarios and Cases
sections.description: Typical analytical situations and question models encountered in competitive examinations.

cases.condition: Comparison of two or more entities
results: Distinct lines with unique colors, markers, or patterns are plotted for each individual entity.
Visual overlaps allow for quick identification of which entity dominates in a specific parameter.
A visually larger enclosed polygon area generally indicates a higher or better overall performance across all metrics.
Data points plotted closer to the center origin indicate a decline, lower score, or poorer performance in that specific area.
